newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adtranz forms China joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Adtranz forms China joint venture.

text.p: European railway firm Adtranz said on Tuesday that it had formed a joint venture with China's Changchun Car Company to produce rolling stock for mass transit systems.
The new company, to be called Changchun Adtranz Railway Company Ltd, will be formed on January 1, 1997. Adtranz will have a 51 percent stake and Changchun 49 percent.

The joint venture, the first of its kind in China, will manufacture, assemble and test metro trains, light rail vehicles, multiple units and aluminium car body shells, Adtranz said in a statement. Its annual capacity will be 160 vehicles.
Adtranz is a 50-50 joint venture between Daimler-Benz AG and Swiss/Swedish ABB. Changchun is owned by the Chinese ministry of railways and employs 15,000 workers.
Adtranz's China operations has orders to provide 120 metro vehicles for the city of Guangzhou, as well as 210 units for Shanghai's second Metro Line.
